CRAN multibias description even says: "Simultaneous multi-bias analysis can be used to enhance the validity and transparency of real-world evidence obtained from observational,...The problem statement is still accurate on the core point: the tools exist in isolation without a unified workflow, and the absence of agreed protocols for ordering, reporting contributions, and resolving conflicts remains unresolved. opinions.rationale: Inverted-prior search treated the gap as already closed and looked for a field-standard emulation pipeline that declares negative controls, treatment/outcome proxies, proximal identification, instruments, and validation samples in the protocol, reports what each tool bought on a shared estimand, and reconciles disagreements. That standard was not found. The cited works (Hubbard–Hernán 2024; Hernán–Robins 2016) correctly locate residual confounding outside protocol design; they do not integrate residual-confounding tools into a workflow. Recent literature and software add components and occasional applications, not a consensus order or combination rule. Guo et al. (2025) run a target trial emulation under proximal causal inference with declared NCE/NCO proxies and sensitivity swaps of those controls: that is a serious applied fusion of TTE and PCI, not a field standard or a protocol template for combining PCI with E-values, bias functions, Rosenbaum models, tipping points, and external validation on one estimand. BenchExCal (Wang et al. 2025) proposes a structured benchmark–expand–calibration process that uses negative-control calibration in an emulation pipeline; the paper is a design and planned evaluation, not an established convention. Practical TTE checklists and operational EHR frameworks (e.g., Tran 2026; Nature Digital Medicine operational TTE 2026) recommend negative-control diagnostics, which softens the claim that residual tools are invisible in guidance, but still treat them as optional diagnostics rather than protocol-declared primary analyses. TARGET (JAMA 2025) is a reporting checklist for emulations; it does not prescribe proximal protocols or multi-tool reconciliation. CRAN task-view and package checks (TrialEmulation, gfoRmula, gfoRmulaICE, lmtp, ltmle, WeightIt, MatchIt, cobalt, PCL) show no merged standard that wires NCO panels, proximal estimation, validation-sample correction, and conventional estimands into one emulation API. Distributional NCO diagnosis/calibration work on medRxiv (2026) is a proposal. Sensitivity and proximal methods still rest on untestable, non-identical identification stories; papers that propose or apply methods do not solve combination under disagreement. Covariate balance remains widely reported without claiming identification of unmeasured confounding in the sources retrieved. Queries run: TTE+proximal; NCO calibration/BenchExCal/TARGET; PCI software (PCL, regression-based PCI); package/CRAN activity for TrialEmulation/gfoRmula/lmtp; guidance (TARGET, ENCePP, ICH). Net: the problem as stated (no agreed integrated residual-confounding workflow for emulations) remains open; the caveat is that TTE+PCI applications and NCO-centric calibration proposals now exist and should be cited as prior art, not as closure.

counter_evidence.quote: We integrated the target trial emulation (TTE) framework with the proximal causal inference (PCI) approach, a novel method proposed to correct unmeasured confounding through the use of negative controls as measured proxies of unmeasured confounders.

This paper proposes a benchmark, expand, and calibration (BenchExCal) approach to trial emulation and describes the design and process for evaluating the performance of this approach through simulation studies and five planned empirical examples.

opinions.rationale: The agenda claim that there is little theory for joint violations is not faithful. Multi-bias quantitative bias analysis is textbook material (Lash–Fox–Fink), with simultaneous adjustment methods, multiple-bias bounds, and released software. Smith, Mathur, and VanderWeele (2021) give composite bounds for unmeasured confounding, selection, and differential exposure/outcome misclassification and explicitly warn that one-at-a-time analysis can misstate joint impact. Brendel, Torres, and Arah (2023) develop simultaneous multi-bias adjustment via imputation and/or regression weighting for uncontrolled confounding, selection bias, and misclassification together; the CRAN package multibias (v1.7.3, still maintained 2026) implements that framework and advertises use for observational longitudinal real-world evidence. The EValue ecosystem documents multiple-bias bound examples. Gerlach-Wood et al. (2025) review QBA software and catalog tools that adjust several bias sources simultaneously (multibias, episensr variants, others), while still noting gaps and uneven simultaneous versus sequential implementations. For longitudinal time-varying treatment settings closer to sustained-strategy emulation, Tan (2025, Biometrika) formulates multi-period sensitivity models under sequential unmeasured confounding and contrasts joint versus product sensitivity models, which directly engages the report’s point that product-of-marginals can be the wrong answer. These works partially deliver the proposed direction: modular bias parameters, joint regions or adjusted estimates under several systematic errors, and (in probabilistic QBA) separation of systematic from sampling uncertainty. They do not fully close the problem as stated for a complete longitudinal g-methods target trial emulation in which unmeasured confounding, selection, measurement error, and practical positivity failure all enter one modular identification region reported as standard practice. Gao et al. (2025, Biometrics) still describe joint multi-assumption sensitivity for externally controlled trials as largely unexplored outside their omnibus contribution, which is useful counterweight to over-claiming full solution. No journal mandate for joint identification regions in TTE was found; professional cost of wide regions remains a social, not a mathematical, barrier. Package checks of TrialEmulation/gfoRmula/lmtp did not show native multi-bias identification-region reporting. So the correct status is partial solution of the joint multi-bias theory/software agenda for standard observational designs, with residual open work for full sustained-strategy TTE g-method modules and for ID-region-versus-sampling-interval reporting as a field norm. The claim of little joint theory is overstated relative to Smith–VanderWeele bounds, Brendel simultaneous multi-bias, multibias software, and Tan’s joint longitudinal sensitivity models.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Theory and software exist for joint multi-bias analysis of confounding, selection, and misclassification (and for some longitudinal sequential-confounding sensitivity models), but modular joint identification regions that also include practical positivity failure under sustained-strategy g-methods are not yet a standard, required part of target trial emulation reporting, and product-of-marginals approximations remain the default in practice.

resolving_work.title: Multiple-bias Sensitivity Analysis Using Bounds
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Gives a composite bound and sensitivity analysis for the joint impact of unmeasured confounding, selection bias, and differential exposure or outcome misclassification on a risk ratio, with explicit warning that one-at-a-time analysis can under- or over-state joint bias; implements the multiple-bias bound in the EValue tooling.
resolving_work.quote: By failing to consider multiple biases at once, researchers can underestimate—or overestimate—their joint impact. We show that it is possible to bound the total composite bias owing to these three sources and to use that bound to assess the sensitivity of a risk ratio to any combination of these biases.

resolving_work.title: Simultaneous adjustment of uncontrolled confounding, selection bias and misclassification in multiple-bias modelling
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Proposes simultaneous (not merely sequential) multi-bias adjustment for uncontrolled confounding, selection bias, and misclassification via imputation and/or regression weighting, evaluated as a joint alternative to one-bias-at-a-time analysis.
resolving_work.quote: A novel, alternative approach to multiple-bias adjustment involves the simultaneous adjustment of all biases via imputation and/or regression weighting.

resolving_work.title: multibias: Multiple Bias Analysis in Causal Inference (CRAN package)
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Released, maintained R software that simultaneously adjusts for any combination of uncontrolled confounding, exposure/outcome misclassification, and selection bias, based on Brendel et al. (2023), and marketed for observational longitudinal real-world evidence.
resolving_work.quote: The functions can simultaneously adjust for any combination of uncontrolled confounding, exposure/outcome misclassification, and selection bias. ... Simultaneous multi-bias analysis can be used to enhance the validity and transparency of real-world evidence obtained from observational, longitudinal studies. Based on the work from Paul Brendel, Aracelis Torres, and Onyebuchi Arah (2023) doi:10.1093/ije/dyad001.

resolving_work.title: Sensitivity models and bounds under sequential unmeasured confounding in longitudinal studies
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Develops multi-period sensitivity models and sharp/conservative bounds for longitudinal causal effects under sequential unmeasured confounding, and formulates joint versus product sensitivity models, addressing interaction of time-indexed assumption violations rather than a single one-at-a-time parameter.
resolving_work.quote: We consider sensitivity analysis for causal inference in a longitudinal study with time-varying treatments and covariates. ... joint and product sensitivity models

counter_evidence.quote: However, joint sensitivity analysis for multiple assumptions remains largely unexplored to the best of our knowledge.
